title: Release Scout tactical notes
content:
Purpose: capture lightweight, operational heuristics for the Release Scout role — a rotating person responsible for early-stage micro-exposures and fast feedback during cross-functional rollouts. Not a full runbook, this is a working scratchpad for the team to iterate on ceremony, signals, and immediate play actions.

Context & motivation:
- We run many tiny LL M releases and feature experiments (partial traffic, model variant swaps, hybrid routing). We need a thin layer of human-in-the-loop ownership that is faster than full oncall but more disciplined than ad-hoc watch.
- Release Scout = 1 engineer (product/infra/observability) + 1 product steward as backup. Scout owns the first 60–120 minutes after micro-exposure and performs triage and immediate mitigations.

Quick charter (what Scout does in first 2 hours):
1) Preflight verify: dashboards loaded, canary slices assigned, synthetic probe schedule validated.
2) Watch initial signal sweep (latency, 95/99 p50 deltas, error spikes, token-level cost anomalies, safety classifier rate).
3) Run mini-interventions: scale-back slicing, route specific cohorts to fallback model, flip soft fallback, pause canary traffic if threshold breached.
4) Communicate: ping stakeholders in #release-scouts + call on-call if escalates. Log actions to experiment ticket (JIRA).

Preflight checklist (minutes before exposure) — shorthand:
- Who: Scout + steward named in ticket (JIRA: assignee).
- Dashboards: open traffic-slice view, latency by model, cost-per-token, safety-rate, user-complaint stream.
- Synthetic probes: smoke probe passes (happy-path), adversarial probe queued.
- Traffic target: confirm slice size and expected qps.
- Fallback: confirm fallback model/tag and auto-rollover route exists.
- Rollback path: documented quick-revert instructions (k8s patch / routing toggle).
- Communication: release slack thread prepped, pager rotation noted.

Signal thresholds (working heuristics, tune per-product):
- Latency: +30% p95 sustained for 3 minutes -> alert to scout. +50% -> pause exposure.
- Errors: 2x baseline for request errors or >0.5% absolute increase -> investigate.
- Safety classifier: any increase in high-severity classification >0.1% absolute -> immediate pause and human review.
- Quality regressions (semantic evals): drop in eval score >3 points on calibration prompts -> escalate to model owner.
- Cost: sudden +40% token cost per session for a cohort -> throttle slice.

Triage playbook (first actions in order):
1) Reproduce locally with captured request (if available) or run synthetic probe.
2) Check routing: was traffic misrouted to heavier model variant? If yes -> switch to expected variant.
3) Check capacity: GPU queue depth, OOMs, infra errors. If infra-related -> route to lower-cost model or reduce concurrency.
4) Safety spike: isolate offending cohort(s) or backfill to strictly-moderated path.
5) If ambiguity remains: reduce slice to 10% and keep monitoring; call for pause only if signals persist.

Standard communication snippets (Slack):
- Pre-exposure: "Scout on deck: Aisha. Opening slice=2% at 16:00 PT. Dashboards: <link>. Will monitor 0–2h."
- On incident: "Scout: observed p95 latency +45% on slice A (user cohort mobile-uk). Scaling down slice to 0.5% and routing to fallback-model-v2. Logging actions in JIRA-ROLL-874."
- Post-rewind: "Action: rolled back variant -> stable. Followups: collect sample set and tag for eval. Owner: Lina to investigate prompt distribution"

Mini-automation suggestions (low effort to reduce human noise):
- Auto-run smoke probe 30s after activation; deliver results to slack thread.
- If latency > X and errors > Y within 60s, auto-scale slice down by 50% (requires product approval).
- Synthetic canary generator to exercise rare edge prompts once per 10k requests.

Experiment tagging & observability hygiene (must dos):
- Tag logs/traces with experiment_id, slice_id, scout_name.
- Ensure sampling for traces includes tail latencies and safety-labeled requests.
- Provide a lightweight evaluation prompt set (50–200 items) for the Scout to run quickly after exposure if quality concerns arise.

Escalation ladder (fast path):
- Scout -> product steward (phone/DM) for ambiguous quality issues.
- Steward -> model owner + infra SRE if evidence points to model/regression/infra.
- If user-facing degradation >1% or safety high-severity events -> page SRE and compliance lead.

Post-exposure follow-ups (within 48h):
- Scout writes 1-paragraph incident log: what observed, actions taken, evidence links (traces, sample prompts).
- Product steward schedules a 30-min triage: categorize root cause (model/data/infra/traffic), assign owners, and list next steps.
- Archive the sample set in experiments bucket with experiment_id tag.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Define exact numeric thresholds per region (APAC vs NA may have different baselines).
- How to automatically surface cohort slices with nonstandard prompt distributions before rollout? (input: heuristics engine?).
- Explore a lightweight CLI for scouts to flip common toggles (route, slice size, fallback) with audit log.
- Backtest thresholds against recent 3 months of canary runs and refine.

References & quick links:
- Monitoring dashboard template: https://grafana.redwood/company/rollouts/canary-suite
- Experiment tracking: JIRA-ROLL board (https://jira.redwood/browse/ROLL)
- Rollout toggle service: github.com/redwood-inference/traffic-orchestrator

Notes to self (messy):
- Keep scout role light — not second oncall. Rotation once/week recommended for product teams.
- Create a short training doc + 15-min playbook walkthrough for new scouts.
- Consider pairing Scout with a metrics engineer for the first 3 exposures.

Signoff: iterative draft. If this resonates, convert to paired checklist + small automation backlog ticket.
